Bill.BriefDescription: Revising criteria for reimbursement to counties for extraordinary criminal justice costs.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to reimbursement to counties for extraordinarycriminal justice costs; amending RCW 43.330.190; adding a new sectionto chapter 2.70 RCW; and recodifying RCW 43.330.190.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 43.330.190 and 1999 c 303 s 1 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Counties may submit a petition for relief to the office of publicdefense for reimbursement of extraordinary criminal justice costs.Extraordinary criminal justice costs are defined as those associatedwith investigation, prosecution, indigent defense, jury impanelment,expert witnesses, interpreters, incarceration, and other adjudicationcosts of ((aggravated murder)) one or more homicide cases that have hadan extraordinary and disproportionate impact on the county's budget forthe prior or current year. (1) The office of public defense, in consultation with theWashington association of prosecuting attorneys and the Washingtonassociation of sheriffs and police chiefs, shall develop procedures forprocessing the petitions, for auditing the veracity of the petitions,and for prioritizing the petitions. Prioritization of the petitions p. 1 SSB 6300shall be based on, but not limited to, such factors as disproportionatefiscal impact relative to the county budget, efficient use ofresources, and whether the costs are extraordinary and could not bereasonably accommodated and anticipated in the normal budget process. (2) Before January 1st of each year, the office of public defense,in consultation with the Washington association of prosecutingattorneys and the Washington association of sheriffs and police chiefs,shall develop and submit to the appropriate fiscal committees of thesenate and house of representatives a prioritized list of submittedpetitions that are recommended for funding by the legislature.
RCW 43.330.190 is recodified as a section inchapter 2.70 RCW.
